title: Selected MICrONS pairs leave a response reliability bias in connection direction uncertain
abstract: We tested whether one-way synaptic connections point toward cells with more reliable movie responses in one MICrONS mouse. Both cells had to have measured contact opportunity toward the other cell. The complete sample had 128 pairs from 96 cells. A directional logistic model adjusted for two opportunity-length ratios, layer, and area group. The reliability odds ratio was 1.662 per standardized unit, with a nominal 95 percent cell bootstrap interval of 0.265 to 25.342. Of the connections, 61 pointed toward the cell with higher raw CCmax. The mean target-minus-source CCmax was -0.00701, with interval -0.04528 to 0.03294. The data leave the direction effect uncertain. They do not show a zero effect. Selected cells, one mouse, possible reconstruction error, measurement error, unmeasured cell traits, and unstable bootstrap fits limit inference. Code, source hashes, derived pairs, uncertainty draws, a figure, and retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Direction odds ratios and nominal 95 percent cell bootstrap intervals in one mouse. All intervals include one. Raw CCmax uses a different unit.

citations.reason: Prior reliability and input-count result motivates a conditional direction test; no code or derived data reused.
